q-112325:
To find the value of $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{3}),$ we need to find the number that is located in row $3$ and position $3$ of Pascal's triangle. 

**Important**: When counting the rows and positions in Pascal's triangle, we always start counting from zero! Remember:

- The top row of Pascal's triangle is row $0.$

- The first position of each row (the one of the left) is position number $0.$

The value located in row $3$ and position $3$ is highlighted below.

$$
\begin{aligned} &  &  &  &  &  & 1 \\  &  &  &  &  & 1 &  & 1 \\  &  &  &  & 1 &  & 2 &  & 1 \\  &  &  & 1 &  & 3 &  & 3 &  & 1 \\  &  & 1 &  & 4 &  & 6 &  & 4 &  & 1 \\  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{3})=1.$

$$
\begin{aligned} &  &  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{0}{0}) \\  &  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{1}) \\  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{1}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{2}) \\  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{3}) \\  &  &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1})$ is the sum of the two closest numbers located in the previous row. So,

$$

q-113617:
The binomial coefficient $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{r})$ is given by the formula

$$
(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{r})=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

In this case, we have $n=6$ and $r=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{2}) & =\frac{6!}{(6-2)!\cdot 2!} \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 5\cdot 4!}{4!\cdot 2!} \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 5\cdot \cancel{4!}}{\cancel{4!}\cdot 2} \\  & =\frac{30}{2} \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$
